name: Graphdiyne-like network, large
description: Benzene rings (1,3,5) linked only through butadiyne: ring-C#C-C#C-ring, exactly two alkynes per strut, as in graphdiyne, built as an amorphous 3D network. Built large: a 60 A cell with 8 seeds, then ten passes, each growing 60 blocks, joining clusters twice (so the seeds' clusters become one or two large frameworks), zipping and a rigid-body optimisation with dihedrals (GAFF 1.81, params/gaff_carbon); then a closing phase: three rounds of a wide zip (3.0 A, 110 degrees, clash-checked) and an all-atom (flexible) optimisation, which closes rings, including across the periodic boundary so the framework spans the cell, and lets the blocks flex (docs/closing.md); then Poreblazer on a 0.3 A grid (about 340 MB). Sized for a Slurm node (resources); sweep the cell size or grow counts to go larger. See docs/carbon-families.md.
